ops.content:
The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. To restart the daemon, the caller issues:

```
launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>
```

The `-k` flag kills any running instance before relaunching, making the operation idempotent. This replaces the previous approach of spawning a subprocess directly via Popen, which did not guarantee clean teardown of the old process before the new one started.

ops.content: Daemon restarts are triggered via `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>` rather than a direct Popen spawn. The `-k` flag kills any existing instance before relaunching, ensuring a clean restart. The service target follows the launchd label convention (e.g. `gui/<uid>/com.brain.daemon`). This replaced the previous Popen-based approach in June 2026 as part of an architecture change to bring the daemon fully under launchd supervision, enabling proper lifecycle management, crash recovery, and log routing through the system journal.
